Definition: from δεός (dread); timid, i.e. (by implication) faithless:--fearful.
BiblicalUsage: Fearful is the word for the timid, the faithless, the ones who shrink when the storm rises. The disciples are called fearful in the boat, and the fearful are named among those whose part is in the lake of fire. The word binds timidity to unbelief: the fearful are those who do not trust.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the storm still asks the same question: why are you fearful, O you of little faith? The answer is not to try harder, but to trust the One who is in the boat.
